dish.name: Pink Sauce Penne Pasta
dish.description: Al dente penne tossed in a balanced blend of tangy spiced tomato puree and silky cream sauce.

ingredients.name: Red chilli flakes
ingredients.looksLike: dry spicy red bits with seeds

steps.title: Boil the pasta water
steps.text: Pour 600 ml water into a deep pot and add 1/4 tsp salt. Set over high heat until it reaches a vigorous rolling boil.
steps.cameraCheck: Water rolling with large rapid bubbles across the surface.
steps.tip: Covering the pot with a lid brings water to a boil much faster.
steps.videoShot: Top-down view of rapid bubbles surfacing in the pot.
steps.visualCue: Large energetic bubbles breaking continuously across the water surface.
steps.watchOut: Adding pasta before the boil causes the tubes to turn soggy and stick.

steps.title: Cook the penne
steps.text: Add 60 g penne pasta to the boiling water. Cook uncovered for 9 to 10 minutes until al dente, stirring occasionally.
steps.cameraCheck: Pasta pieces moving freely in simmering water without sticking to the base.
steps.tip: Taste a pasta tube around 8 minutes to check firmness.
steps.videoShot: Close-up of penne gently bobbing in salted boiling water.
steps.visualCue: Penne swells slightly while maintaining its structured tubular shape.
steps.watchOut: Overcooking will make the penne split and become mushy.

steps.title: Reserve water and drain
steps.text: Scoop out 2 tablespoons of starchy pasta water and set aside. Pour the rest through a colander to drain the penne.
steps.cameraCheck: Bowl containing reserved cloudy pasta cooking liquid next to drained penne.
steps.tip: Never rinse cooked pasta under tap water as that washes away starches.
steps.videoShot: Medium shot of penne draining into a sink colander.
steps.visualCue: Steam billowing from drained penne with cloudy cooking liquid safely set aside.
steps.watchOut: Discarding all pasta water leaves you with no way to emulsify the sauce later.

steps.title: Saute the minced garlic
steps.text: Heat 10 ml olive oil in a skillet over medium flame. Add 10 g finely minced garlic and fry for 30 seconds until aromatic.
steps.cameraCheck: Garlic bits gently sizzling in pale oil without browning.
steps.tip: Keep the heat medium-low to avoid burning the delicate garlic.
steps.videoShot: Angled close-up of garlic sizzling quietly in shimmering oil.
steps.visualCue: Garlic turns fragrant and pale golden without dark brown edges.
steps.watchOut: Burnt garlic turns black and infuses the entire dish with a bitter taste.

steps.title: Simmer the tomato puree
steps.text: Pour in 80 g tomato puree, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp oregano, and 1/4 tsp chilli flakes. Simmer on low heat for 4 minutes until thickened.
steps.cameraCheck: Red sauce bubbling gently and thickening along the pan edges.
steps.tip: Stir frequently so the sauce cooks evenly and reduces raw acidity.
steps.videoShot: Top-down view of red puree simmering with herb specks.
steps.visualCue: Puree darkens to a deep crimson and tiny oil droplets separate at borders.
steps.watchOut: High flame makes red puree splatter across the counter and scorch.

steps.title: Blend in fresh cream
steps.text: Lower heat completely and pour in 30 ml fresh cream. Stir continuously until the red puree transforms into a silky blush-pink sauce.
steps.cameraCheck: Sauce showing a uniform pastel pink shade with no dairy separation.
steps.tip: Whisk gently while pouring to ensure uniform texture.
steps.videoShot: Close-up of white cream swirling into red sauce to create pink tint.
steps.visualCue: Color shifts smoothly into a glossy, velvety salmon-pink tone.
steps.watchOut: Excessive heat can split cold cream into watery curds.

steps.title: Toss penne in pink sauce
steps.text: Add drained penne and 1/4 tsp black pepper powder to the sauce. Pour the reserved 2 tablespoons pasta water and toss gently for 1 minute.
steps.cameraCheck: Penne tubes completely coated in glistening pink sauce.
steps.tip: Shake the skillet gently rather than roughly mashing with a spoon.
steps.videoShot: Medium shot of penne sliding through creamy pink sauce.
steps.visualCue: Lustrous pink sauce clings tightly to both outside ridges and hollow centers.
steps.watchOut: Boiling too vigorously now will evaporate liquid and dry out the pasta.

steps.title: Garnish with grated cheese
steps.text: Turn off heat and sprinkle 15 g grated cheese over the pasta. Stir gently so the cheese melts through, then serve hot.
steps.cameraCheck: Melted cheese forming stretchy glossy threads through warm pasta.
steps.tip: Serve immediately while warm to prevent the cream sauce from stiffening.
steps.videoShot: Close-up of finely grated cheese melting into warm penne.
steps.visualCue: Cheese softens immediately and melts into the steaming pasta.
steps.watchOut: Adding cheese over high active heat can turn it rubbery or oily.

healthiness.reason: Offers balanced carbohydrates and moderate protein, but contains refined grains and saturated fats from dairy cream.
swaps: Use whole wheat or chickpea penne to boost dietary fibre.
Substitute full cream with hung curd or blended silken tofu to reduce saturated fat.

dish.batchNote: Easily doubled or tripled using a wider skillet to ensure uniform simmering.
dish.leftoverRemix: Bake leftover pasta topped with a little mozzarella in an oven toaster grill for a quick pasta bake.
dish.storage: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days; loosen with a splash of warm water when reheating.
